newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open up but News, CRA drag.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open up but News, CRA drag.

text.p: Australian shares opened just firmer on Wednesday but with losses in media giant News Corp and major miner CRA limiting any other gains.
At 10.20 a.m. (2320 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 3.3 points up at 2,346.8.

Shares in Rupert Murdoch's News Corp followed its ADRs lower after U.S. broker Goldman Sachs downgraded the stock following its disappointing first quarter results. News Corp shares were 12 cents lower at A$6.83 (US$5.38) at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT).
Miner CRA trailed its dual-listed partner, RTZ Plc, lower after a bearish report on the future of the aluminium market.
Other motivating factors remained elusive. Brokers said there was little to drive the broader local market with many investors just staying away.
"It seems to be a bit of a featureless week so far, with not a lot of activity," said a dealer at a Brisbane brokerage.
"No-one seems to want to buy equities at the moment and I think a lot of that is probably nervousness about the U.S. market," he added, pointing to yet another Dow record high.
"Everyone is wondering when the bubble might burst. People think there will be a pull back there that will flow through to here, so they are just sitting on their hands."
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about 11 to five, while about 48 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
